workingTitle: Solar Orbiter traced a magnetic switchback back to the Sun
freshness: Peer-reviewed Nature Astronomy paper and ESA release published 2026-10-08; preferred 15-day window.
coreFacts: Solar Orbiter flew through one unusually large magnetic switchback while roughly halfway between Earth and the Sun.
Its Solar Wind Analyser measured charged oxygen and carbon whose composition pointed to hot closed magnetic loops in the solar corona.
The team connected the in-situ measurements with solar images and magnetic-field modeling, tracing the plasma to interchange reconnection between closed and open field regions.
The authors infer that interchange reconnection released the switchback, while waves and turbulence shaped its later propagation through the solar wind.
The evidence comes from one exceptionally large switchback, so the result does not establish that every switchback forms in the same way.
caveats: The detailed source reconstruction concerns one unusually large switchback.
The Nature Astronomy article is peer reviewed; the full paper page was access-restricted in the research environment, but its indexed abstract and the complete ESA author release were read.
